reference_sql:
SELECT CAST(order_ts AS DATE) AS order_day, COUNT(*) AS web_orders
FROM orders
WHERE channel = 'web'
  AND CAST(order_ts AS DATE) >= DATE '2026-01-05' - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND CAST(order_ts AS DATE) < DATE '2026-01-05'
GROUP BY 1
alternatives: SELECT CAST(order_ts AS DATE) AS order_day, COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'web' AND CAST(order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-06' AND DATE '2026-01-04' GROUP BY 1

SELECT CAST(order_ts AS DATE) AS order_day, COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'web' AND order_ts >= DATE '2026-01-05' - INTERVAL 30 DAY AND order_ts < DATE '2026-01-05' GROUP BY CAST(order_ts AS DATE)

other_way.sql: SELECT CAST(order_ts AS DATE) AS order_day, COUNT(*) AS web_orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'web' AND CAST(order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-12-06' AND DATE '2026-01-04' GROUP BY 1
other_way.tradeoff: Typing both end dates with BETWEEN reads clearly, but counting back from the as-of date shows where the 30 days come from.
